facts.fact: FBI 上门：Dr. Cooper 与 Agent Burke 属 FBI 领导的任务组，监控并「管理」镜子穿越。
facts.anchor: We’re from an FBI-led task force that monitors and…” He pauses, squinting as he searches for words. “…regulates time travel through the mirrors.

facts.fact: 他们派了特工 Gibbons 去找 Ben 和 Clara，但出了事——两人回来了，Gibbons 没回来。
facts.anchor: We sent an operative after the two of you, but something went wrong. You’re here and he’s not,” Burke says.

facts.fact: FBI 小镜测试：Clara 一分钟内手就沉进去（能量惊人）；Ben 的能量量级很低。
facts.anchor: Within a minute, my hand sinks through the surface.

facts.fact: Cooper 理论：镜子会残留「潜伏能量」，Ben 当年的掉入可能是镜子自发排能。
facts.anchor: I theorize that the mirror spontaneously opened for Mr. Mitchell as a way of expelling its unused energy.

facts.fact: 穿越规则：镜子提供 A 到 B 通道——制造年代附近 ↔ 现代（或被毁年代）。
facts.anchor: the mirrors provide an A-to-B type passageway from near the time of their making in the past to either the present or near the time they were destroyed

facts.fact: Gibbons 1928 年出现在纽约（面部追踪软件扫历史照片）；他们要 Clara 带队去接他。
facts.anchor: Gibbons showed up on our facial tracking software in 1928,

facts.fact: 威胁：拒绝协助则资金冻结甚至没收——Ben 的财富是「未经授权穿越的收益」。
facts.anchor: Your funds are likely to be tied up for a while and possibly confiscated since they were the benefit of unauthorized travel.

facts.fact: Clara 表态：她一辈子都能感到镜子的能量（一直以为是静电）——「我们可能是拯救世界的人」。
facts.anchor: I can feel it—the energy when I touch mirrors. I’ve felt it all my life, but I thought it was weird static electricity or something.

facts.fact: Cooper 力挺 Ben：两年没触发任何警报，比 Burke 这种「按手册训练」的更胜任。
facts.anchor: He spent two years in the past and never set off any of our protocols. He’s far more trained than you are for this.

facts.fact: 章末：两人被送上大飞机——1928 纽约任务开始。
facts.anchor: Okay, time to stop treating us like prisoners and more like members of the team.
